# Diagnostics and Triage
## Handheld analyzer
1. Take [color=#58e6d9]HandheldHealthAnalyzer[/color]. 2. Use it on the patient. 3. Wait for the diagnostics window to open.
Shows approximate ranges for oxygen, blood, and perfusion, plus pressure, rhythm, pain, shock, consciousness, external bleeding, and available signs of damage to body regions.
## Full scan
1. Place and buckle the patient into [color=#58e6d9]MedicalScanner[/color]. 2. Open the nearby [color=#58e6d9]computerBodyScanner[/color] console. 3. Select medical diagnostics.
Shows exact wounds, internal bleeding, fractures, structural damage, organ function, drugs, cyberware, and active operations.
## Interface sections
- [color=#58e6d9]Priority triage feed[/color] — active threats in priority order. - [color=#58e6d9]Vital telemetry[/color] — oxygen, blood, perfusion, pressure, rhythm, pain, and shock. - [color=#58e6d9]Regions[/color] — body region damage and function. - [color=#58e6d9]Wounds[/color] — type, severity, bleeding, contamination, infection, and applied treatment. - [color=#58e6d9]Organs[/color] — integrity and function of internal organs. - [color=#58e6d9]Cyberware[/color] — integrity, power, temperature, EMP, and neural link. - [color=#58e6d9]Drugs[/color] — concentration, therapeutic effect, and toxic load of drugs.
## Triage priority
1. Massive or arterial external bleeding. 2. No breathing or circulation, critical hypoxia. 3. Internal bleeding, vital organ damage, critical shock. 4. Open fracture, tendon rupture, nerve damage, or vessel damage. 5. Stable wound, infection, pain, and planned surgery.
After an intervention, repeat the scan and check the new state revision.
